text: Track 3.1 My name's Frida Robinson and I write a blog about travel trends. I'm going to look at a couple of recent trends in flight travel. Has anyone in the audience been on a very long flight? I thought so. You probably noticed that these flights are longer than ever. There is now a direct flight from London to Perth in Australia, for example. It takes 17 hours and extreme amount of time to be sitting on an airplane. And that isn't the longest flight. Do you know what the longest flight is? Well, it's from Singapore to New York and it takes 19 hours. Would you want to sit on a plane for 19 hours to avoid changing planes 2 or 3 times? I know I would. Direct flights are more convenient because you buy one ticket, fly with one airline, and you save time by not having to queue at 2 or 3 security points. Also, you don't have to wait around for your flight to board and take off. I think long direct flights will be more common in the future, as airlines have started focusing their attention both on safety and comfort. Plains now have high ceilings, better seats and bigger windows. But you are still on a plane for 17 to 19 hours. What are the airlines trying to do about this? Well, boom, an American startup company are making supersonic planes. They want to reduce the flight between LA and Sydney from 15 hours to 7, and the flight from San Francisco to Tokyo from 11 to just 5 hours. I believe there will be a serious change in long distance travel when these planes become available. Tickets might be expensive at first, but prices will go down when more airlines join in. Moving on to another trend now. Who here knows what FOMO is? Young people, people born between 1981 and 1996, called millennials, probably know. Fear of missing out. But what does FOMO have to do with flight trends? Well, it's to do with independent travelers who want to experience new things. Things their friends haven't done yet. And a lot of millennials are making travel choices based on social media, especially Instagram. These types of travelers are looking for one of a kind experiences, and airlines are trying to take advantage of this. Experts say that about 40% of travelers under 33 years old are checking the Instagram ability of their holiday destinations, as they want something cool to share on social media. This means airlines are increasing the number of destinations we can fly to, and they are making it easier to get there too. So, some of the ways the travel industry is changing are more direct flights with longer flight times, airlines attempts to reduce these, and an increase in unusual destinations. If you want to check out more travel trends, then visit my blog at www.
